```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Daryani 2016 built three linked models to choose and then check a pediatric
dose of intravenous bolus 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) for recurrent ependymoma. All
three are packaged:

| Model | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| `Daryani_2016_fluorouracil_mouse` | Mouse plasma PK, tumor extracellular fluid (tECF) PK and tumor growth inhibition, fitted to mouse data (Table 1). |
| `Daryani_2016_fluorouracil_scaled_adult` | Simulation model used for dose selection: the adult Terret 2000 plasma model, normalised to body surface area (Supplementary Table 1), driving the mouse tECF and tumor-growth models (Figure 4). |
| `Daryani_2016_fluorouracil` | Pediatric population PK fitted to the phase I trial (Table 2), linked to the mouse tECF model to predict tumor exposure. |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Daryani_2016_fluorouracil"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12075> (open access, with the authors'
  NONMEM control streams as Supplementary Material 9)

All three models use hours for time, give plasma and tECF 5-FU in uM, and
convert the mg dose with the 5-FU molecular weight 130.08 g/mol.

# Population

**Mouse.** CD1 nude mice. Plasma PK came from non-tumor-bearing mice given
75 mg/kg as an i.v. bolus (n = 4) or as a 3-day subcutaneous infusion (n = 5);
tECF PK from cerebral microdialysis in mice bearing orthotopic mEP Ephb2
ependymoma (75 mg/kg bolus, then 13 mg/kg/h for 24 h); and tumor growth from
luciferase bioluminescence in three efficacy experiments (55 mice), normalised to
each animal's value 7 days after implantation (Supplementary Material 1).

**Children.** 26 children and young adults with recurrent or refractory
ependymoma in a phase I trial (median age 7.1 years, range 3.8-21.1; 18 girls;
19 White, 5 Black, 2 other; median weight 25.5 kg, range 10.8-83.0; median BSA
0.9 m^2, range 0.6-2.0; Supplementary Table 2), given 400, 500 or 650 mg/m^2
5-FU as an i.v. bolus, 570 plasma concentrations.

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Daryani_2016_fluorouracil")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. Summary:

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Mouse plasma `vmax`, `km`, `vc`, `q`, `vp` | 2040 umol/h/kg, 125 uM, 0.962 L/kg, 1.67 L/h/kg, 0.332 L/kg | Table 1, plasma PK study |
| Mouse `fu` | 0.366 | Supplementary Material 9 (`FU = 0.366`); Table 1 prints 0.37 |
| `vecf` | 0.001 L/kg (mouse), 0.001 L/m^2 (human) | Table 1 V3,m; Results text |
| `kin_ecf`, `kout_ecf` | 0.00426, 3.24 1/h | Supplementary Material 9 K13, K31; Table 1 |
| `kin_int_tumor`, `kout_int_tumor` | 1.82, 0.334 1/h | Table 1 K34,m, K43,m |
| `vmax_ecf`, `km_ecf` | 0.00633 umol/h/kg, 0.0107 uM | Supplementary Material 9 K30, KM2; Table 1 |
| `kgrow`, `e_study_exp23_kgrow` | 0.158, +0.102 1/h | Table 1; Equations 7-9 |
| `kgrow_lin`, `psi` | 214,000 1/h, 0.0936 | Table 1; Equation 1 |
| `kmax`, `ec50`, `hill` | 0.658 1/h, 2.12 uM, 1.22 | Table 1; Equation 6 |
| `ktr` | 0.946 1/h | Table 1 Kdel,m; Equations 2-4 |
| Mouse IIV | 12.2, 22.1, 31.1, 7.8, 26.1, 40.6, 30.4 % CV | Table 1 |
| Mouse residual error | 35.9, 27.9, 37.0 % | Table 1 |
| Scaled-adult `vmax`, `km`, `vc`, `k12`, `k21` | 5773 umol/h/m^2, 42.8 uM, 7.4 L/m^2, 5.35, 5.69 1/h | Supplementary Table 1 |
| Human `fu` | 0.9 | Results, 'Application of scaled-adult model' |
| Pediatric `cl`, `vc`, `q`, `vp` | 16.6 L/h/m^2, 4.2 L/m^2, 1.6 L/h/m^2, 20.1 L/m^2 | Table 2 |
| Pediatric IIV / IOV | 28.8, 26.6, 80.1, 93.9 % CV; IOV on CL 13.0 % CV | Table 2; Supplementary Material 9 occasions |
| Pediatric residual error | additive 1.98 uM, proportional 0.51 | Table 2; Supplementary Material 9 `$ERROR` |
| tECF ODE `d/dt(ecf)` | `kin_ecf * fu * central - ...` | Supplementary Material 9 `DADT(3)` |
| Tumor ODEs | | Equations 1-6 |

# Mouse model

```{r mouse-setup}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Daryani_2016_fluorouracil_mouse")
mw <- 130.08
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)

# One cohort of n mice; `dose_rows` is a data frame of dosing records.
mouse_cohort <- function(n, dose_rows, obs_times, arm, exp23 = 0, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, dose_rows) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  # The model has three endpoints (Cc, Cecf, tumor_size), so observation rows
  # carry a dvid; every observable is returned on every row regardless.
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(STUDY_EXP23 = exp23, arm = arm) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

# Typical-value solve. rxode2 warns when several subjects are solved without
# omega; that is the intent here (one subject per arm), so only that warning
# is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(mod, events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega"), events = events, ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}
```

## Plasma and tumor ECF PK (Figure 2)

```{r mouse-pk}
pk_events <- bind_rows(
  mouse_cohort(200, data.frame(time = 0, amt = 75, dur = 0),
    c(0, seq(1 / 12, 3, by = 1 / 12)), "75 mg/kg i.v. bolus"),
  mouse_cohort(200, data.frame(time = 0, amt = 75, dur = 72),
    c(0, seq(2, 72, by = 2)), "75 mg/kg 3-day infusion", id_offset = 200L),
  mouse_cohort(200, data.frame(time = 0, amt = 13 * 24, dur = 24),
    c(0, seq(0.5, 24, by = 0.5)), "13 mg/kg/h for 24 h", id_offset = 400L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(pk_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
pk_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, events = pk_events, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 6}
pk_sim |>
  select(arm, time, Plasma = Cc, `Tumor ECF` = Cecf) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Plasma, `Tumor ECF`), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(arm, matrix, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), Q50 = median(conc), Q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 7.1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(matrix ~ arm, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "5-FU (uM)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Daryani 2016 (median and 5th-95th percentiles; dotted line: 7.1 uM in vitro IC90)."
  )
```

The text gives plasma steady-state means of 7.11 +/- 2.64 uM (24-h infusion at
13 mg/kg/h) and 0.43 +/- 0.18 uM (3-day infusion), tECF above the 7.1 uM target
for about 1 hour after the bolus, and infusion tECF at least sevenfold lower.

```{r mouse-pk-checks}
mouse_typ <- solve_typical(mod_mouse, pk_events |> filter(id %in% c(1L, 201L, 401L)), keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame()
css_24h <- mouse_typ$Cc[mouse_typ$arm == "13 mg/kg/h for 24 h" & mouse_typ$time == 24]
css_3d <- mouse_typ$Cc[mouse_typ$arm == "75 mg/kg 3-day infusion" & mouse_typ$time == 72]
bolus <- mouse_typ[mouse_typ$arm == "75 mg/kg i.v. bolus" & mouse_typ$time > 0.2, ]
t_above <- max(bolus$time[bolus$Cecf >= 7.1])
cecf_inf <- mouse_typ$Cecf[mouse_typ$arm == "13 mg/kg/h for 24 h" & mouse_typ$time == 24]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Quantity = c(
      "Plasma Css, 13 mg/kg/h (uM)", "Plasma Css, 3-day infusion (uM)",
      "Last time tECF >= 7.1 uM after bolus (h)", "tECF at 24 h of 13 mg/kg/h (uM)"
    ),
    Model = signif(c(css_24h, css_3d, t_above, cecf_inf), 3),
    Paper = c("7.11 +/- 2.64", "0.43 +/- 0.18", "about 1", "about 7-fold below 7.1")
  ),
  caption = "Typical-value mouse predictions against the values stated in the Results."
)
stopifnot(
  abs(css_24h / 7.11 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(css_3d / 0.43 - 1) < 0.35,
  t_above > 0.5, t_above < 1.5,
  # The Results say at least sevenfold below the bolus target; the model gives
  # about 6.8-fold, so the gate checks the order of magnitude.
  cecf_inf < 7.1 / 5
)
```

## Tumor growth inhibition (Figure 3)

Time zero is day 7 after implantation, when the bioluminescence was normalised
to 1. Bolus arms are dosed weekly for 4 weeks; the infusion arms of experiment
two get a 3- or 5-day infusion of 75 mg/kg every 3 weeks.

```{r mouse-tgi}
tgi_obs <- seq(0, 33 * 24, by = 6)
bolus_wk <- function(amt) data.frame(time = c(0, 168, 336, 504), amt = amt, dur = 0)
inf_q3w <- function(days) data.frame(time = c(0, 504), amt = 75, dur = days * 24)
no_dose <- data.frame(time = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0)
tgi_arms <- list(
  list("Exp 1", "Control", no_dose, 0),
  list("Exp 1", "75 mg/kg bolus weekly", bolus_wk(75), 0),
  list("Exp 2", "Control", no_dose, 1),
  list("Exp 2", "75 mg/kg 3-day infusion q3w", inf_q3w(3), 1),
  list("Exp 2", "75 mg/kg 5-day infusion q3w", inf_q3w(5), 1),
  list("Exp 3", "Control", no_dose, 1),
  list("Exp 3", "75 mg/kg bolus weekly", bolus_wk(75), 1),
  list("Exp 3", "37.5 mg/kg bolus weekly", bolus_wk(37.5), 1)
)
tgi_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(tgi_arms), function(i) {
  a <- tgi_arms[[i]]
  mouse_cohort(100, a[[3]], tgi_obs, a[[2]], exp23 = a[[4]], id_offset = (i - 1L) * 100L) |>
    mutate(experiment = a[[1]])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(tgi_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
tgi_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, events = tgi_events, keep = c("arm", "experiment")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
tgi_sim |>
  group_by(experiment, arm, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.05), Q50 = median(tumor_size),
    Q95 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(day = time / 24 + 7) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ experiment + arm, ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after implantation (days)", y = "Fold change in bioluminescence",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Daryani 2016 (median and 5th-95th percentiles of individual predictions)."
  )
```

Figure 3 shows control medians of roughly 150 (experiment one) and 400
(experiments two and three) at day 40, and about 20 for the weekly 75 mg/kg
bolus of experiment one; the infusions have no visible effect. The Discussion
gives a tumor growth delay of 16-19 days for 75 mg/kg weekly bolus versus
control, measured at the control animals' day-28 (median survival) tumor burden
(Supplementary Figure 3).

```{r mouse-tgi-checks}
# One typical animal per arm, followed to day 57 so the treated tumors can
# reach the control day-28 burden.
typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(tgi_arms), function(i) {
  a <- tgi_arms[[i]]
  mouse_cohort(1, a[[3]], seq(0, 50 * 24, by = 6), a[[2]], exp23 = a[[4]], id_offset = i - 1L) |>
    mutate(experiment = a[[1]])
}))
typ_tgi <- solve_typical(mod_mouse, typ_events, keep = c("arm", "experiment")) |>
  as.data.frame()
w_end <- typ_tgi |>
  filter(time == 33 * 24) |>
  select(experiment, arm, tumor_size)
knitr::kable(w_end, digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value fold change at day 40.")
growth_delay <- function(exp_name, treated_arm) {
  ctl <- typ_tgi |> filter(experiment == exp_name, arm == "Control")
  trt <- typ_tgi |> filter(experiment == exp_name, arm == treated_arm)
  w28 <- ctl$tumor_size[ctl$time == 21 * 24]
  (min(trt$time[trt$tumor_size >= w28 & trt$time > 504]) - 21 * 24) / 24
}
delays <- c(
  exp1 = growth_delay("Exp 1", "75 mg/kg bolus weekly"),
  exp3 = growth_delay("Exp 3", "75 mg/kg bolus weekly")
)
delays
w <- setNames(w_end$tumor_size, paste(w_end$experiment, w_end$arm))
stopifnot(
  w[["Exp 1 Control"]] > 75, w[["Exp 1 Control"]] < 300,
  w[["Exp 2 Control"]] > 200, w[["Exp 2 Control"]] < 900,
  w[["Exp 1 75 mg/kg bolus weekly"]] > 8, w[["Exp 1 75 mg/kg bolus weekly"]] < 50,
  # Infusions: no more than a 30% reduction against control.
  w[["Exp 2 75 mg/kg 3-day infusion q3w"]] > 0.7 * w[["Exp 2 Control"]],
  all(delays > 13), all(delays < 22)
)
```

## Plasma NCA

```{r mouse-nca}
# Sampling design of the bolus plasma study: 5, 15, 30, 60 and 120 min.
nca_mouse <- pk_sim |>
  filter(arm == "75 mg/kg i.v. bolus", !is.na(Cc)) |>
  filter(time == 0 | round(time * 60) %in% c(5, 15, 30, 60, 120)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)
dose_mouse <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1, arm == "75 mg/kg i.v. bolus") |>
  mutate(amt = amt * 1000 / mw) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm)
nca_res_mouse <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_mouse, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_mouse, amt ~ time | arm + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 1 / 12, end = 2, cmax = TRUE)
))
published_mouse <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax,
  "75 mg/kg i.v. bolus", 536
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res_mouse,
  reference = published_mouse,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "uM"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mouse plasma Cmax (first sample at 5 min) against the Results mean of 536 +/- 162 uM. * differs by >20%.")
```

The simulated median 5-minute concentration is about a quarter below the
reported mean Cmax and inside its standard deviation. The paper does not say
which samples the mean was taken over; the microdialysis mice were first
sampled at 3 minutes, where the typical prediction is about 470 uM against 400 uM
at 5 minutes, so the earlier samples alone would close half the gap. The Figure 2a visual
predictive check is the fuller comparison.

# Scaled-adult model and dose selection (Figure 4)

The scaled-adult model is deterministic: the paper gives no between-subject
variability for it (Figure 4's band uses the Terret 2000 adult variability,
which Daryani 2016 does not report). Concentrations do not depend on BSA when
the dose is in mg/m^2, so a BSA of 1 m^2 is used.

```{r scaled-qualification}
mod_sa <- readModelDb("Daryani_2016_fluorouracil_scaled_adult")
# Qualification: 80 mg/m^2/h for 12 h; the authors simulated a mean
# steady state of 4.1 uM against 6.7 uM observed in children.
qual <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sa,
  events = data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = c(0, 6, 11, 12), evid = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 0L),
    amt = c(960, 0, 0, 0), dur = c(12, 0, 0, 0), cmt = "central",
    BSA = 1, STUDY_EXP23 = 0
  )
) |>
  as.data.frame()
css_ped <- qual$Cc[qual$time == 11]
css_ped
stopifnot(css_ped > 6.7 / 2, css_ped < 6.7 * 2)
```

```{r scaled-sim}
sa_events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(c(400, 500, 650)), function(i) {
  d <- c(400, 500, 650)[i]
  obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(0, 45 * 24, by = 4))))
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = c(0, 168, 336, 504), evid = 1L, amt = d),
    data.frame(time = obs, evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(
      id = i, cmt = "central", BSA = 1, STUDY_EXP23 = 0,
      dose = paste(d, "mg/m^2")
    )
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sa_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sa, events = sa_events, keep = "dose") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 6}
p_top <- sa_sim |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 2) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cecf)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 7.1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "tECF 5-FU (uM)")
p_bottom <- sa_sim |>
  mutate(day = time / 24 + 7) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, tumor_size)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Fold change in bioluminescence",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Daryani 2016 (typical values; first dose on day 7)."
  )
print(p_top)
print(p_bottom)
```

```{r scaled-table}
sa_summary <- sa_sim |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(
    cecf_peak = max(Cecf[time <= 2]),
    cecf_1h = Cecf[time == 1],
    delay_days = min(time[tumor_size >= 1 & time > 504]) / 24,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(paper_delay_days = c(29, 31, 33))
sa_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = dose,
    "Peak tECF (uM)" = cecf_peak,
    "tECF at 1 h (uM)" = cecf_1h,
    "Model growth delay (days)" = delay_days,
    "Figure 4 growth delay (days)" = paper_delay_days
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Scaled-adult typical-value predictions. Growth delay is the time from the first dose until the tumor burden returns to its starting value.")
stopifnot(all(sa_summary$cecf_1h > 7.1), all(diff(sa_summary$delay_days) > 0))
```

The model ranks the doses as the paper does and every dose keeps the typical
tECF above 7.1 uM at 1 hour, but its typical tECF is several-fold above the
Figure 4 median (peak about 100 uM in Figure 4) and its growth delays are about
10 days longer than the labelled 29, 31 and 33 days; see Assumptions and
deviations.

# Pediatric population PK (Table 2, Figure 5)

```{r ped-cohort}
# The inter-occasion etas enter clearance through occasion indicators, which
# rxode2 reports as not mu-referenced; that is expected for this structure, so
# only that warning is muffled when the model is parsed.
mod_ped <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Daryani_2016_fluorouracil")),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("non-mu referenced", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
ped_cohort <- function(n, dose_m2, id_offset = 0L) {
  # BSA: log-normal around the 0.9 m^2 median, kept inside the 0.6-2.0 m^2 range.
  bsa <- pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(0.95), 0.3)), 0.6), 2.0)
  subj <- data.frame(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), BSA = bsa)
  obs_t <- c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8)
  bind_rows(
    subj |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_m2 * BSA),
    tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_t) |> mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", OCC = 1L, regimen = paste(dose_m2, "mg/m^2")) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
set.seed(2016)
ped_events <- bind_rows(
  ped_cohort(200, 400),
  ped_cohort(200, 500, id_offset = 200L),
  ped_cohort(200, 650, id_offset = 400L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ped_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
ped_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ped, events = ped_events, keep = c("regimen", "BSA")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-5}
ped_sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = median(sim), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 0.1), ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma 5-FU (uM)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5d-f of Daryani 2016 (VPC with residual error; dashed line: 15 uM LLOQ)."
  )
```

## Predicted tumor exposure

The paper simulated each patient's tECF profile from their post hoc estimates:
every patient on every occasion reached the 7.1 uM target at 1 hour, with a
median (range) of 182.5 (51.8-754.1) uM.

```{r ped-tecf}
tecf_1h <- ped_sim |>
  filter(time == 1) |>
  pull(Cecf)
round(c(median = median(tecf_1h), quantile(tecf_1h, c(0.05, 0.95))), 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(tecf_1h) / 182.5 - 1) < 0.35,
  quantile(tecf_1h, 0.05) > 7.1
)
```

## Pediatric plasma NCA

```{r ped-nca}
nca_ped <- ped_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
dose_ped <- ped_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(amt = amt * 1000 / mw) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)
nca_res_ped <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_ped, Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ped, amt ~ time | regimen + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
    half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
  )
))
ped_nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res_ped) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
ped_nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = regimen,
    "Cmax (uM)" = cmax,
    "AUCinf (uM*h)" = aucinf.obs,
    "Half-life (h)" = half.life,
    "CL (L/h)" = cl.obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated NCA by dose (the paper reports no pediatric NCA).")
# Clearance per m^2 from NCA should sit near the Table 2 value of 16.6 L/h/m^2.
cl_m2 <- as.data.frame(nca_res_ped) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.obs") |>
  left_join(distinct(ped_sim, id, BSA), by = "id") |>
  mutate(cl_m2 = PPORRES / BSA)
median(cl_m2$cl_m2)
stopifnot(abs(median(cl_m2$cl_m2) / 16.6 - 1) < 0.15)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Values the PK-PD control stream holds versus Table 1.** The mouse tumor
  growth parameters were estimated with the plasma and tECF parameters held at
  the values in the authors' PK-PD control stream (Supplementary Material 9).
  Those are used: K13 = 0.00426 (Table 1: 0.0043), K30 = 0.00633 (0.0063),
  fu = 0.366 (0.37) and KM2 = 0.0107 uM, where Table 1 prints 0.012 uM. The
  KM2 difference matters only at tECF concentrations near 0.01 uM.
- **Table 1 unit typo.** V3,m is printed in L/hr; it is a volume, 0.001 L/kg.
- **Microdialysis fractions.** The authors fitted each 30-min or 4-h dialysate
  fraction as its own accumulating compartment (`MTIME`). The packaged model
  gives the instantaneous tECF concentration; a fraction equals its mean over
  the collection interval (the control stream applies no recovery correction).
  The tubing lag mentioned in the Methods is not in the control stream.
- **Mouse plasma residual error.** Table 1 gives 30.7% for the plasma-only fit
  and 35.9% for the joint plasma + tECF fit; the joint value is used.
- **Experiment three doses.** The main text and Figure 3 give 75 and 37.5 mg/kg;
  Supplementary Material 1 says 57 and 37 mg/kg. The main text is followed.
- **Number of microdialysis mice.** Not stated.
- **Human tECF link.** The control stream writes the tECF input as
  `K13 * C1 * V1 * FU`, with V1 the plasma central volume, and V3 = 0.001. For
  the human models the maintainers kept that form with the human V1 and V3 =
  0.001 on the same per-m^2 scale as V1 (multiplied by BSA here). With the
  pediatric model this reproduces the reported median 1-hour tECF of 182.5 uM.
- **Scaled-adult model does not reproduce Figure 4 quantitatively.** With the
  same link, the typical tECF peaks near 800-1400 uM against about 100 uM for the
  Figure 4 median, and the tumor burden falls further than Figure 4 shows. The
  paper does not say how the tECF volume was scaled to humans for Figure 4. The
  maintainers tested other readings: keeping the mouse V1 in the tECF input
  matches the Figure 4 tECF peak but not its growth delays, and no reading
  reproduced both panels and the pediatric result. The model is packaged in the
  control-stream form and the difference is recorded here.
- **Scaled-adult variability and growth rate.** No variability is included,
  because the Terret 2000 variances used for Figure 4 are not reported in
  Daryani 2016. Which mouse experiment's growth rate Figure 4 used is not
  stated; `STUDY_EXP23 = 0` (experiment one) is the default.
- **Pediatric occasions.** Occasions 1-3 each have their own IOV eta on CL and
  every later occasion shares a fourth, as in the control stream. The virtual
  cohort uses occasion 1.
- **Pediatric BLQ handling.** The 15 uM LLOQ and M3 method matter only for
  fitting; simulations return all concentrations.
- **Virtual pediatric cohort.** BSA was drawn log-normally around the reported
  0.9 m^2 median and kept within the reported 0.6-2.0 m^2 range; age, sex and
  race do not enter the model.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for Daryani 2016 was found on Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-24.
